newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CHANG, MARTIN SURVIVE SCARES IN MEMPHIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG, MARTIN SURVIVE SCARES IN MEMPHIS.

text.p: Third seed Todd Martin remained on course to reach his fifth consecutive Memphis final after surviving a tough challenge from France's Guillaume Raoux in the third round of the St Jude tournament on Thursday.
Two-time champion Martin was stretched to a third-set tie-break before prevailing 6-4 6-7 7-6 in a two-hour and 11-minute serve and volley slugest with the 93rd-ranked Raoux.
Top seed Michael Chang also needed three sets to reach the quarter-finals.
Chang dropped a first-set tie-break 2-7 to 15th seed Kenneth Carlsen of Denmark before taking control for a 6-7 6-2 6-0 victory.

Other seeds advancing to the quarters with third-round wins Thursday were fifth seed Paul Haarhuis of the Netherlands, seventh-seeded American Richey Reneberg, eighth-seeded Australian doubles star Todd Woodbridge and number 13 Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden.
Unseeded American Jeff Tarango took a pair of tie-breaks to oust Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten, who had stunned second seed Andre Agassi in the second round.
Chang, attempting to reach his first Memphis final in his 10th year playing here, said things started to fall in place after he broke Carlsen to go up 2-1 in the second set.
"It was pretty important to break him. When you do that it is going to play on a big server's mind," said Chang, who reeled off 10 of the last 11 games to set up a quarter-final with Reneberg.
The 14th-ranked Martin faced the possibility of allowing Raoux to serve for the match, but instead saved three break points while serving at 5-5 in the third set.
When the set reached the tiebreaker, Martin gave away nothing, pounding winners to reach 6-0 before the Frenchman ended it on a double fault.
Martin, a crowd favourite here because of his past success in Memphis, said the fans helped him through the third-set crisis.
"Out there I was getting emotional at 5-5 in the third set," said the 1994 and 1995 champion. "It felt like the Davis Cup instead of the third round of the Kroger St. Jude."
